# dorm22

> Multiplies a general matrix by a banded orthogonal matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dorm22 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dorm22';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dorm22( order, side, trans, M, N, n1, n2, Q, LDQ, C, LDC, WORK ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `OperationSide` | in |  | one of `'left'`, `'right'` | specifies the operation type |
| `trans` | `("no-transpose"\|"transpose")` | in |  | one of `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the operation type |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `n1` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `n1 < 0 \|\| n1 + n2 !== (side === 'left' ? M : N)` | n2 is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. |
| `n2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `n2 ≥ 0` | n2 is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. |
| `Q` | `Float64Array` | in | `(side === 'left' ? M : N) × (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDQ ≥ max( 1, side === 'left' ? M : N )` | leading dimension of `Q` |
| `C` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDC` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDC ≥ max( 1, M )`; row-major requires `LDC ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `C` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ n1 === 0 \|\| n2 === 0 ? 1 : (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |  | output array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'L'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Left;
  -   `= 'R'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Right.
- `trans`:

  -   `= 'N'`: apply Q (No transpose);
  -   `= 'C'`: apply $Q^T$ (Conjugate transpose).
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix C. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix C. $N \ge 0$.
- `n2`: N1 is INTEGER `N2` is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. N1, $N_{2} \ge 0$. The following requirement must be satisfied: $N_{1} + N_{2} = M$ if `SIDE = 'L'` and $N_{1} + N_{2} = N$ if `SIDE = 'R'`.
- `Q`: (`LDQ`,N) if `SIDE = 'R'`
- `C`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix C. On exit, C is overwritten by $Q \, C$ or $Q^T \, C$ or $C \, Q^T$ or $C \, Q$.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `n1 < 0 \|\| n1 + n2 !== ( side === "left" ? M : N )`)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, side === 'left' ? M : N )`
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dorm22.ndarray(
    side, trans,
    M, N,
    n1,
    n2,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    C, strideC1, strideC2, offsetC,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | `OperationSide` | in |  | one of `'left'`, `'right'` | specifies the operation type |
| `trans` | `("no-transpose"\|"transpose")` | in |  | one of `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the operation type |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `n1` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `n1 < 0 \|\| n1 + n2 !== (side === 'left' ? M : N)` | n2 is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. |
| `n2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `n2 ≥ 0` | n2 is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. |
| `Q` | `Float64Array` | in | `(side === 'left' ? M : N) × (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Q` |
| `C` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideC1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `C` |
| ↳ `strideC2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `C` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `C` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ n1 === 0 \|\| n2 === 0 ? 1 : (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'L'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Left;
  -   `= 'R'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Right.
- `trans`:

  -   `= 'N'`: apply Q (No transpose);
  -   `= 'C'`: apply $Q^T$ (Conjugate transpose).
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix C. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix C. $N \ge 0$.
- `n2`: N1 is INTEGER `N2` is INTEGER The dimension of Q12 and Q21, respectively. N1, $N_{2} \ge 0$. The following requirement must be satisfied: $N_{1} + N_{2} = M$ if `SIDE = 'L'` and $N_{1} + N_{2} = N$ if `SIDE = 'R'`.
- `Q`: (`LDQ`,N) if `SIDE = 'R'`
- `C`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix C. On exit, C is overwritten by $Q \, C$ or $Q^T \, C$ or $C \, Q^T$ or $C \, Q$.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `n1 < 0 \|\| n1 + n2 !== ( side === "left" ? M : N )`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `M === 0 || N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dorm22()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DORM22`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dorm22.f).
-   The orthogonal matrix `Q` is assumed to have a 2x2 block structure: an upper-left rectangular block, a lower-triangular block, an upper-triangular block, and a lower-right rectangular block. It is typically produced by the multi-shift QR iteration (`dlaqr2`/`dlaqr3`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import uniform from '@stdlib/random/array/uniform/lib/index.js';
import dorm22 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dorm22';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};

const M = 5;
const N = 4;
const n1 = 3;
const n2 = 2;

const Q = uniform( M * M, -1.0, 1.0, opts );
const C = uniform( M * N, -1.0, 1.0, opts );
const WORK = uniform( M * N, 0.0, 1.0, opts );

const info = dorm22( 'column-major', 'left', 'no-transpose', M, N, n1, n2, Q, M, C, M, WORK );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( C ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORM22`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORM22 overwrites the general real M-by-N matrix C with

|   | `SIDE = 'L'` | `SIDE = 'R'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TRANS = 'N'`: | $Q \, C$ | $C \, Q$ |
| `TRANS = 'T'`: | $Q^T \, C$ | $C \, Q^T$ |

where Q is a real orthogonal matrix of order NQ, with $\mathrm{NQ} = M$ if `SIDE = 'L'` and $\mathrm{NQ} = N$ if `SIDE = 'R'`. The orthogonal matrix Q processes a 2-by-2 block structure

$$
Q = \begin{bmatrix} Q_{11} & Q_{12} \\  &  \\ Q_{21} & Q_{22} \end{bmatrix}
$$

where Q12 is an `N1`-by-`N1` lower triangular matrix and Q21 is an `N2`-by-`N2` upper triangular matrix.

</section>
